To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed an effective method of detecting the saliency of objects in photos and that this method can be used to objectively assess the privacy risks of the visual information contained in the salient objects.
we have proposed a novel saliency detection algorithm for locating objects and extracting saliency information from photos.

we propose a saliency detection and a visual privacy assessment method for photos that are based on a combination of a patch-based salient object detection method and an improved risk assessment system, and we show that our method is effective for detecting saliency information in a photo and for quantitatively assessing the visual privacy levels of objects in a picture.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of assessing the influence of visual privacy information on photo privacy protection.
the visual privacy of objects in a photograph.
the problem of quantitatively evaluating the privacy risk of visual information in photos.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed saliency detection and privacy assessment methods are both effective.

the proposed computational privacy assessment system provides a scientific method for objectively assessing the visual privacy levels of objects in a photograph and for quantitatively evaluating the influence of visual information on the privacy of objects.
the saliency detection of objects is a useful method of quantitatively evaluating visual privacy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide a computational framework to objectively assess the visual privacy levels of objects in photos.

we propose a computational privacy assessment method that can effectively and objectively evaluate the visual privacy levels of objects in photos and provide guidance for the protection of photo privacy.
we propose a novel method to quantitatively assess the privacy levels of objects in photos by combining the visual saliencies and object categories of these objects.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the visual saliencies of objects in a photograph can be used to quantitatively assess the levels of visual private information that the objects contain.
visual saliency is a key factor that influences the privacy risk of objects in photos and can therefore be used for the assessment of visual privacy levels.
the proposed saliency detection and computational privacy assessment methods can provide objective, scientific, and quantitative guidance to the design of privacy protection algorithms.
